title: Dugnad
reading: Dugnad is voluntary unpaid work. Dugnad work is a community effort. It is a common form of work in clubs and associations. In a housing cooperative, for example, the residents often take part in a dugnad in spring to tidy up after the winter. It is common in many kindergartens for the parents to get together for a dugnad once or several times a year. Then they might wash the kindergarten’s toys or fix up the outdoor areas.

Many children in Norway take part in organised leisure activities, and many of the activities are run by the parents as a dugnad. The parents could e.g. organise a jumble sale or a cultural event to raise money for the association.
Dugnad is an old custom in Norway. There is a similar tradition in most farming communities around the world.
discussion: Talk together What are your thoughts on dugnad? Are you already familiar with the concept? Have you ever been invited to take part in a dugnad in Norway? Some clubs and associations practise an arrangement where you can pay a certain amount to not take part in a dugnad. What do you think about that? It’s Monday. Two fathers are picking up their children from kindergarten. They are talking about the weekend’s dugnad at the kindergarten. Henrik: Nice to see you again! It was amazing how much we got done! The new playhouse turned out great! Arne: Yes. It’s so nice to work together like that too. But Truls’ parents never come to any dugnad. Henrik: I’ve noticed that too. Although it’s voluntary, it still doesn’t look good. Arne: Yes. I realise there can be times when it doesn’t suit, but every time...? Henrik: Mm. And I’m sure that Truls will use the playhouse just as much as the other children. Talk about the above situation. Why do Henrik and Arne react in the way they do? What do you think the consequence may be of not taking part in dugnad? GettyImages
exercises: Select the right answer What is Dugnad? Work you have to do in your job without being paid. Voluntary, unpaid work. Paid work for voluntary organisations. Select the right answer What are typical dugnad jobs in a kindergarten? Make timetables for the employees and pay bills. Wash toys and fix up the outdoor areas. Take the children to a museum. Select the right answer Who normally organises a dugnad? sports clubs leisure activities for children enterprises housing cooperatives Select the right answer Is dugnad a phenomenon that is unique to Norway? Yes, dugnad was invented in Norway, and is only found in Norway. No, there is a similar tradition in many farming communities. No, but dugnad is only found in countries in Scandinavia. Select right or wrong Read the statements. What is right? What is wrong? In 2004, the word ‘dugnad’ was voted Norway’s national word. Right Wrong Many leisure activities for children are run by parents based on dugnad. Right Wrong Dugnad is common in enterprises and paid workplaces. Right Wrong People are paid by the hour for taking part in a dugnad. Right Wrong Many housing cooperatives have a dugnad to make the outdoor area look nice after the winter. Right Wrong Select the right image Which images show typical dugnad jobs? You can select more than one image.
teacher_notes: Lærerinnhold Tips til undervisningen De fleste deltakere vil kjenne til dugnad i en eller annen form. Dugnad i storfamilien eller i naboskapet er kanskje noe de har vært med på. Vil dugnad i f. eks. barnehagen eller i borettslaget oppleves like forpliktende og selvfølgelig? Hva skal til for at man skal føle seg forpliktet? Kan deltakelse i dugnad føre til at man knytter nye kontakter og får et større nettverk? Se filmen Videoen består av ti klipp som illustrerer dugnadsarbeid. De første seks klippene viser vanlige dugnadsoppgaver: barn og voksne som raker en hage, mennesker som plukker søppel og planter blomster, og et klipp fra et loppemarked. Deretter vises klipp av vafler med syltetøy og kaffe i pappkopper, som er typisk norsk dugnadsmat. Videoen avsluttes med to klipp av et par som maler bord sammen, og en gjeng som gir hverandre high fives etter å ha satt opp en vegg i fellesskap. Forslag til spørsmål Har dere dugnad, eller noe som ligner, i ditt hjemland? Hva er positivt med dugnad? Har du vært på dugnad? Hva gjorde dere? Snakk sammen Selv om dugnad i utgangspunktet er frivillig, vil de fleste føle seg forpliktet til å delta. Det blir også forventet at en deltar. Vil det snakkes om de som ikke deltar? På hvilken måte? Hva om det er de samme som ikke stiller opp hver gang? Snakk om konsekvenser ved ikke å delta i et slikt fellesskap (snakk, utenforskap, manglende tilhørighet i lokalmiljøet, manglende integrering osv.) Diskuter om disse konsekvensene også gjelder for andre arenaer (f. eks. oppmøte på foreldremøter, følge barn på fritidsaktiviteter, sosiale tilstelninger på jobb osv.)
